verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the software rule that a no-referral mint assigns a prize ticket to a randomly selected existing NFT holder.
The client specifies that no-referral allocation includes the $5 commission and both current prize-ticket types.
Eliminating Big Blocks necessarily removes the Big Block ticket from the no-referral reward allocation while retaining the commission and Small Block ticket.
The client identifies an unresolved system edge case because the first mint has no existing NFT holder eligible to receive its random rewards.
The client extends random reward allocation to mints supplying either no referral code or an invalid referral code.
First concrete failure on the USDC no-referral path: the completed mint generated no randomly allocated prize ticket.
The client confirms random allocation of the no-referral commission but leaves the corresponding ticket requirement materially unresolved.
Target-specific implementation claim that no-referral mints now generate a ticket and randomly assign the commission.
The client establishes the executable accounting rule of one commission and one ticket per successful primary mint, excluding secondary sales.
The client accepts the system-enforced first-mint exception because no prior NFT holder exists to receive its commission or ticket.
The client acceptance resolves the outstanding first-mint allocation uncertainty and returns the Requirement to active implementation.
First concrete verification after the fix: the client completed the requested no-referral test of ticket and commission behavior and reported that it worked perfectly.
